public_holidays: 2027-06-18: Juneteenth (official: fixed 19 June in the Code of Virginia; a Saturday in 2027, so the preceding Friday is the holiday)
2027-10-11: Columbus Day and Yorktown Victory Day (official: both on the second Monday in October under section 2.2-3300)
2027-11-02: Election Day (official: Tuesday after the first Monday in November is a legal holiday)
2027-11-26: Friday after Thanksgiving (official: part of the Thanksgiving holiday in section 2.2-3300)
Official note: the Code lists George Washington Day on the third Monday in February; the Governor may appoint further holidays.

laws.rule: Drivers may not hold a hand-held phone or other personal communications device while driving a moving vehicle on Virginia highways (Code 46.2-818.2). It is allowed when lawfully parked or stopped, and to report an emergency.
laws.penalty_signal: US$125 for a first offence, US$250 for a later one, and a mandatory US$250 in a highway work zone (about A$178 and A$355 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040).

laws.rule: Using a radar detector in a vehicle on Virginia highways is unlawful, and so is selling one in Virginia (Code 46.2-1079). A detector found in a vehicle on the highway is treated as evidence of use, even if it was not switched on, unless it had no power source and was not within reach of anyone in the vehicle. Police may take the device as evidence; no licence points apply.

items.text: Adults 21 and over may have up to 2 ounces (about 57 g) of marijuana on them or in a public place (Code 4.1-1100). Having more than 2 ounces brings a civil penalty of up to US$25; more than 4 ounces is a crime. Possession at home is not capped in the same way.

No one may consume marijuana in a public place (Code 4.1-1108). Until 1 July 2027 the first offence is a civil penalty of up to US$25 (about A$36 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040); from 1 July 2027 it rises to up to US$250 (about A$355). A third offence is a Class 4 misdemeanour.
There are no licensed adult-use cannabis shops yet. House Bill 30 (2026) set up a regulated retail market, which the Virginia Cannabis Control Authority says will open on 1 July 2027.

Since 15 August 2026, a product with more than 2 mg of total THC per package can't be made or sold as hemp in Virginia, and the old rule allowing more THC when enough CBD was present (the 25:1 ratio) has gone. Hemp regulation was due to move from the Department of Agriculture to the Cannabis Control Authority in August 2026.
